pr_title: Enable `EntityRef::get_by_id` and friends to take multiple ids and get multiple pointers back
pr_body:
# Objective

- Closes #15577 

## Solution

The following functions can now also take multiple component IDs and return multiple pointers back:
- `EntityRef::get_by_id`
- `EntityMut::get_by_id`
- `EntityMut::into_borrow_by_id`
- `EntityMut::get_mut_by_id`
- `EntityMut::into_mut_by_id`
- `EntityWorldMut::get_by_id`
- `EntityWorldMut::into_borrow_by_id`
- `EntityWorldMut::get_mut_by_id`
- `EntityWorldMut::into_mut_by_id`

If you pass in X, you receive Y:
- give a single `ComponentId`, receive a single `Ptr`/`MutUntyped`
- give a `[ComponentId; N]` (array), receive a `[Ptr; N]`/`[MutUntyped; N]`
- give a `&[ComponentId; N]` (array), receive a `[Ptr; N]`/`[MutUntyped; N]`
- give a `&[ComponentId]` (slice), receive a `Vec<Ptr>`/`Vec<MutUntyped>`
- give a `&HashSet<ComponentId>`, receive a `HashMap<ComponentId, Ptr>`/`HashMap<ComponentId, MutUntyped>`

## Testing

- Added 4 new tests.

---

## Migration Guide

- The following functions now return an `Result<_, EntityComponentError>` instead of a `Option<_>`: `EntityRef::get_by_id`, `EntityMut::get_by_id`, `EntityMut::into_borrow_by_id`, `EntityMut::get_mut_by_id`, `EntityMut::into_mut_by_id`, `EntityWorldMut::get_by_id`, `EntityWorldMut::into_borrow_by_id`, `EntityWorldMut::get_mut_by_id`, `EntityWorldMut::into_mut_by_id`
pr_comments: Something worth considering: should we return a different error type for the immutable variants, as `EntityComponentError::AliasedMutability` is never returned for them?

issue_context.title: Add `EntityRef::get_components_dyn()` and `EntityMut::get_components_dyn()` to query multiple components
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

The dynamic query API [`World::get_many_entities_dynamic_mut()`](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/ecs/prelude/struct.World.html#method.get_many_entities_dynamic_mut) returns an `EntityMut` which can access all components of an entity... but only one by one. Often you need to access 2+ components at once.

## What solution would you like?

Add the proposed methods which allow retrieving more than 1 component at once.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

There's no alternative possible from user code I think.
comments: One alternative would be a unsafe `get_mut_by_id_unchecked` that takes an `&self`. It'd be a little more awkward to use, but would be maximally flexible.

True. I'd rather have a safer API which validates that I don't request twice the same component though. `get_components_dyn()` can do that, and we can provide an `HashSet`-based variant to skip the check like [`World::get_many_entities_from_set_mut()`](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/ecs/prelude/struct.World.html#method.get_many_entities_from_set_mut).

I still think there should be a `get_mut_by_id_unchecked`. The apis added in #15593 could end up allocating in some tight loops which would be a perf footgun. The unchecked version would allow users to implement their own versions in userspace that could reuse the allocations.

review_comments: Is this `&[ComponentId]` casting necessary because it can't infer?
Correct, it infers as `&[ComponentId; 2]` which would use the array impl.
could use `&vec![x_id, y_id]` it should be closer to a typical use case
I'm curious why we need a separate loop and some uninit? Can't we just build the pointers directly?
To be able to get a same-sized array back, the alternative would be [`std::array:try_map`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.array.html#method.try_map), however it's currently unstable.
Document that the check is O(n^2) quadratic? Probably not a blocker given it's a number of unique components, so likely small, but still maybe worth the user being aware.

Note for discussion: I found myself on the `World` API, which is similar, wanting an overload which takes as input a `HashMap<ComponentId, T>` for any `T`. The hashmap keys have the same unicity guarantee as a `HashSet` but there's no way to obtain the latter from the former without allocating a copy of all keys. And I think it's not uncommon for the caller to have some data associated with each component retrieved, to process them uniformly. Thoughts?

(the core issue here is that Rust is missing some "set" slice so unlike normal slices which can abstract any array-like container, we have to use concrete types like`HashMap` and `HashSet` instead, which means any missing one in the API requires converting to the other available one)
I have been working on an `EntitySet` trait, which would abstract over the property of uniqueness like this. It'll be for `Entity` only, but `ComponentId` will eventually just be `Entity` IIRC.
Might look into doing the same thing for `World` later today
I think one mutable + immutable refs is also invalid access
True, but with the current API it's not possible to request both mutable and immutable references at the same time. You can only receive either all mutable references, or all immutable references.
